title: First history reads and provision retries share a bounded initialization fence
steps: Pause a first history read with a real Git index writer, then run the real provision admission block before releasing the reader.
Hold the provision initialization fence and request history and changes for the same site, then read another site and exercise a contended bounded wait.
Run the actual provision backup branch against a rebuilt SQLite fixture and compare old and new tagged files and database; compare fresh full initial backup behavior.
Queue two established readers behind a normal repo writer, then hold two shared admissions while provision waits for both.
expect: Provision waits before mutation, both baseline operations finish without index.lock errors, and the historical v1 remains unchanged without a rebuilt database trailer.
Contending readers answer building without initializing a repo; another site remains independent, and a bounded wait refuses mutation on timeout.
Reprovision preserves file-only v1 and creates a new full point with matching rebuilt files and database; fresh initial provisioning retains full v1.
Ordinary concurrent readers retain their backup rows without building metadata; exclusive provision admission waits for every shared reader to finish.
fence: stable per-site initialization lock outside the repo, held across provision writes and first-read initialization

cmd: --test-name-pattern=first history read finishing|history and changes during|concurrent established history|provision admission waits|EmDash: (provision retry|the Initial backup)
tests: a first history read finishing before provision mutation cannot race the retry baseline index
history and changes during guarded provisioning return building without initializing a repo
concurrent established history reads wait for the writer without claiming the site is building
provision admission waits until every shared established reader has released its fence
EmDash: provision retry preserves historical v1 and captures rebuilt files and database in a new point
EmDash: the Initial backup builds the repo and puts the database on v1; a second call and a later point leave v1 alone
